attorneys.name: Erin H. Abrams
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Lake Charles, LA
attorneys.bio:
Erin Abrams is an associate attorney focused on domestic law. She was born and raised in Southern California, where attended San Diego State University, played Division I water polo, and was given the opportunity to study abroad at the University of Oxford. Erin completed her Juris Doctorate at the Paul M. Hebert School of Law at Louisiana State University, was an inaugural member of the Order of the Barristers, and member of the Trial Advocacy Board.

Erin is passionate about the courtroom, understanding the unique and emotional situations her clients face, and highly values and protects the trust they place in her integrity and capabilities. She is decisive, strategic, communicates clearly, and always provides an honest assessment of what options exist, key considerations respective to each, as well as where a case stands at any point in the process.

In her free time, Erin enjoys cooking, camping, kayaking, and spending time with friends and family. She currently serves as President of the SWLA Bar Association’s Family Law Section and is a Board Member of both the Louisiana State Bar Association Family Law Section and the SWLA Bar Association’s Executive Council.

attorneys.bio:
Mr. Adams represents clients in various types of business transactions and in commercial litigation matters. He also regularly assists both privately-held companies and start-up businesses with formation, financing, and operations issues.

He received his undergraduate degree in Accounting from the University of New Orleans where he graduated Cum Laude and near the top of his class, and his law degree from Loyola University of New Orleans College of Law where he was a Member of the Loyola Law Review.

Mr. Adams is a frequent instructor at Loyola where he teaches a course on business entity documentation as part of the Skills curriculum and lectures on Business Entities for Loyola’s bar exam preparation supplemental lecture series. He has also presented materials on Advanced L.L.C. Issues to attorneys and business professionals and is a contributing author to Foreign Investment in Real Estate: Louisiana State Q&A, Practical Law by Thomson Reuters.

Mr. Adams serves as a member of Loyola Law School's College of Law Visiting Committee. He also volunteers as a mentor of students for the Entrepreneurship Project at Loyola and has chaired the Business Transactions Law Committee of the New Orleans Bar Association.

attorneys.practice_type: Complex Litigation Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio: Mr. Airey has a broad base of experience, representing a wide array of both domestic and international clients. His litigation experience includes acting as lead trial counsel in federal and state court and before arbitration panels, and performing appellate work in the U.S. Supreme Court, U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, and all Louisiana Appellate courts. In addition to his trial work, Mr. Airey provides business advice and legal guidance to clients regarding business operation and formation, employment matters, mergers, real estate transactions, and risk management. As a former licensed Coast Guard Captain, Mr. Airey also has extensive knowledge of admiralty and maritime matters. In 2019 he was elected unopposed as St. Tammany Parish Councilman for District 13. He also serves on the board for St. Tammany Communication District No. 1, as well as holding executive positions on a number of civic organization boards.

attorneys.name: Bennett Boyd Anderson Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Trucking Accidents Lawyers in Lafayette, LA
attorneys.bio:
Bennett Boyd Anderson, Jr., was raised in Lafayette, LA, graduating from Lafayette High School and University of Louisiana at Lafayette (formerly University of Southwestern Louisiana). He obtained his Juris Doctorate from Tulane Law School in 1975 at age 23. Since 1975, Mr. Anderson has practiced law continuously, specializing in Louisiana plaintiff personal injury and wrongful death litigation from offshore/maritime incidents, auto and workplace accidents. He has personally obtained over $200 million for injured parties through jury trials, judge trials and settlements. He has been an “AV” rated attorney by the Martindale Hubbell Rating Service (highest possible rating) for over 25 years.

He has a Board Certification in Civil Trial Advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy and has been honored as one of the “Best Lawyers in America” (2016-2020). He has been selected as the “Lawyer of the Year” (Personal Injury, Lafayette, LA.) by Best Lawyers in 2020. Mr. Anderson has been designated as one of Louisiana’s outstanding personal injury attorneys (“Super Lawyers”) 2008-2020. He is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum. Mr. Anderson has been awarded the Presidential Award by the Lafayette Bar Association and is a lifetime Charter member of the Rue Ratings “Best Attorneys in America”.

Additionally, Mr. Anderson has served as an officer and/or director of many legal and civic organizations, including the Lafayette General Hospital Foundation (Chairman of Board of Directors, 2018-2020), IberiaBank (Advisory Board, 2002-2020), Lafayette Bar Association (Secretary, Treasurer, Vice-President) and Louisiana Bar Foundation (Board of Directors). He is a member of the Louisiana and American Bar Associations as well as the Louisiana Association for Justice and the American Association for Justice.

Mr. Anderson has exclusively practiced plaintiff personal injury law in the Acadiana area for over 40 years. He has been honored as a speaker many times at personal injury/maritime and personal injury/trial practice seminars.

Mr. Anderson is a sixth-generation Lafayette Parish resident. He maintains his home in Broussard, La., with his wife, Georgette, and three children. He is an Eagle Scout, avid outdoorsman, hunter, youth coach and tennis player.

attorneys.name: Precious Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Lake Charles, LA
attorneys.bio:
Precious Anderson experienced first hand how it feels to not be listened to. A lawyer’s job is to make clients feel heard, and at The Townsley Law Firm, Precious has the opportunity to be a compassionate listener and become that voice for people.

Precious grew up in DeQuincy, Louisiana, attending DeQuincy High School. After high school, she went to McNeese to pursue a degree in elementary education. Precious always wanted to be a lawyer but was unsure of the path she wanted to take and knew that she could teach until she decided to make that leap and become an attorney.

She was passionate about math, so after graduating from McNeese, she taught elementary math for five years. In 2020, Precious decided the time was right to pursue her dream. She began law school at Southern University Law Center.

During her second year of law school, Precious was a part of the Southern University Law Review and received several CALI Awards for criminal law, torts one and two, and basic civil procedure. These awards are given to the student with the highest grade in a specific class and represent academic excellence.

She also worked as a teacher’s assistant and a student attorney in the District Attorney’s office, where she participated in two jury trials. She graduated from Southern in 2023.

While she was working at the DA’s office, a judge recommended that she send her application to The Townsley Law Firm. The firm is family oriented and close knit, so Precious thought she would be a great fit. Joining the TLF family in 2024, Precious has felt the freedom and trust necessary to make the best decisions for her clients.

Outside of the office, Precious is the secretary for the Workers Compensation Section. She loves reading romance and science fiction novels and spending time with her kids. Doing these things outside of work helps her decompress.

Precious has two children, Marcus and Benzi. Some of the most influential people in her life were her high school counselor, Cindy, and her pastor’s wife, Louella, who pushed her to be the best version of herself.

Knowing that her clients need her inspires Precious to get to work everyday. Her goal is to make a real and lasting difference in people’s lives. Even when the work gets hard, Precious knows that her team at TLF has her back and is willing to help.

At The Townsley Law Firm, Precious has become an elite member of the team, winning multiple cases for clients across her practice areas. She strives to do excellent work for her clients every day.

attorneys.name: Shandy Arguelles
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Slidell, LA
attorneys.bio:
I received my undergraduate degree at Louisiana State University in 1999 and my law degree from the Loyola University School of Law New Orleans in 2003. Since then, I've been admitted to practice law in the State of Louisiana.

I clerked for the Honorable Jo Ellen Grant in the 24th Judicial District Court for two years upon graduation and passing the bar. From there, I worked in-house in a corporation which was my dream job. However, I found myself wanting to be in the courtroom. After three years in-house, I decided to hang my own shingle as they say and started my own practice. I had a knack for attracting family law cases so decided to give it my full attention and have never looked back. I consider myself fortunate to have found my niche so early in my law career.

I've successfully handled hundreds of family law cases, including divorce, custody, support, property partitions, adoptions and post-judgment modifications.

I am admitted to practice in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana and all Louisiana state courts. I am a member of the Louisiana State Bar Association, Covington Bar Association including the Family Law Section, a member of the Slidell Bar Association and I am a Certified Child Custody and Visitation Mediator.

Why should this matter to you? I attend conferences through the year by these organizations that keep me up to date on the latest in court developments and family law trends nationwide. This means that I will be prepared to handle issues that may arise in your case. Family law is a complex area of law that is continually changing. You need an attorney who is committed to staying up to date and who fully understands the delicate process of family law cases.

Email me using the form on this website or call 1-877-393-6281 or 985-718-455 to set up a free, no-obligation meeting to talk about how I can help you.

attorneys.name: John T. Arnold
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
Licensed since 2007, John Arnold focuses his practice on environmental law matters. John works with the Jones, Swanson, Huddell & Garrison, LLC environmental litigation team representing various business and property owners against the industry's leading oil and gas operators. Working alongside the firm since 2008, John has handled and will continue to work with cases involving ownership disputes and property damages resulting from oil and gas exploration and production.

John has a rich background in environmental stewardship and natural resource management. While pursuing an undergraduate degree in Wildlife Science at Mississippi State University, he worked on numerous waterfowl research projects throughout the Mississippi Alluvial Valley from Canada to Louisiana. Upon obtaining his Bachelor's degree, John provided consultation to an international corporate client and continued his work related to waterfowl research. In 2005, he completed his education at Mississippi State by earning a Master's degree in Wildlife Science. His graduate studies were focused on ecology and human dimensions with his thesis pertaining to characteristics of wildlife law violators and their attitudes toward conservation officers.

John enrolled in the Mississippi College School of Law in 2004 concentrating mainly on the varied aspects of environmental law. While enrolled in law school, Mr. Arnold consulted with an engineering firm and served as an extern with the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality. Between law school graduation and forming his own firm in 2013, John managed the legal division of a nationally recognized environmental consulting firm and compiled a diverse experience portfolio by working with private individuals and corporate clients and local, state, and federal governments and agencies. His experiences include litigation support related to environmental damages and restoration related to oil and gas exploration and production; however, he has also been heavily involved in litigation related to ownership of water bottoms within Louisiana. John has also evaluated the opportunities and constraints of existing and proposed restoration measures in coastal Louisiana to synthesize measures to conserve wetlands and multiple land uses. He has also assisted with contract review, project planning, and site evaluation and selection of construction for restoration.

John has been involved in several agency actions involving the United States Government, including the protested award of a contract for support services issued by the Department of the Army, Army Corps of Engineers (COE) and Galveston District. John was involved in the challenge of the agency's evaluation of proposals and decisions to award the contract. In his role, he attended agency hearings, filed appropriate protest documentation pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations on behalf of client and responded to COE filings.

REPRESENTATIVE PUBLICATIONS & LECTURES

As a scientist, John has provided expert opinions with nationally renowned scientists with diverse areas of expertise on matters requiring integration of multiple scientific disciplines.

Gagliano, S.M., J. Battle, W. Wilson, J. Arnold, G. Barbee, J. Rogers, and G. Castille. 2011. Investigation of Environmental Impacts of Oil and Gas Activities on the Houssiere Property, Acadia Parish, LA. Expert Report.

Gagliano, S.M., K.M. Wicker, J. Battle, G. Wang, G.J. Castille, and J.T. Arnold. 2010. Navigability Assessment of Stump Lagoon in St. Bernard Parish, Louisiana. Expert Report.

Pearson, C., J.T. Arnold, and M. Tinsley. 2010. Underwater Investigations of Activities Related to Barge-Mounted Drilling Rig Access in East Galveston Bay, Galveston

County, Texas. Expert Report.

attorneys.name: James R. Austin
attorneys.practice_type: Banking and Bank Regulatory Lawyers in Baton Rouge, LA
attorneys.bio:
Jim Austin joined Adams and Reese in 2007 and focuses his practice in the areas of banking and finance, real estate transactions and governance. This includes contracts, large corporate and middle market lending transactions, commercial real estate transactions, asset-based lending transactions, syndicated credits and loan participations, leveraged leases, USDA and SBA guaranteed loans, rate management transactions and marine financing.

With more than 30 years of legal experience both within financial institutions and as outside counsel, Jim also works in the areas of debtor/creditor relations, federal and state banking regulations and governmental relations.

His significant contributions include:

· Serving as lead lawyer in the Banc One Corporation Law Department for Bank One's Private Banking line of business. He supported that line of business across the bank's 12-state footprint.

· Serving as Senior Vice President, Legal Counsel and Assistant Secretary for Premier Bank, National Association - a Louisiana bank with over $4 billion in assets and operations across the entire state. He was part of a very small legal team that supported all of the bank's commercial and retail lines of business. He was also solely responsible for supporting the managed assets department with a portfolio of loans and real estate in excess of $400 million.

· Serving as legal counsel for Premier Bank, National Association and its successor for nearly a decade.

Jim is involved in the recruiting of new attorneys for Adams and Reese and is active in client development. Professionally, he is former Chairman of the Louisiana Bankers Association Bank Counsel Committee and serves on the Louisiana State Law Institute UCC Committee and Security Devices Committee. He also serves on the Board of Directors for the Baton Rouge Area Chamber of Commerce, is a past member of the Baton Rouge Rotary Club and a past President and Board Member of the Baton Rouge Symphony.

In his free time, Jim enjoys time with his family, travel, golf and automobiles.

attorneys.firm_name: Sher Garner Cahill Richter Klein & Hilbert, L.L.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
John T. Balhoff, II, a member of the firm, was born in Baton Rouge, Louisiana in 1971. He attended college at the University of Notre Dame and graduated from there, cum laude, in 1993, receiving a Bachelor of Business Administration degree in finance. Mr. Balhoff received his Juris Doctor degree from the Paul M. Hebert Law Center at Louisiana State University in 1996.

Mr. Balhoff presently is admitted to the Louisiana Bar and he also is admitted to practice before all United States District Courts in Louisiana as well as the United States Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. Mr. Balhoff has experience in trial before Louisiana district courts and in oral arguments before Louisiana's district and appellate courts, including the Louisiana Supreme Court, and before various federal courts, including the United States Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. Mr. Balhoff also has experience in arbitration. His legal practice includes the areas of title litigation, commercial litigation, foreclosures, environmental and toxic tort, insurance defense, premises liability, securities litigation, construction litigation and automobile liability. He is a member of the Federal, New Orleans, Louisiana State and American Bar Associations.

Mr. Balhoff is a former member of the Board of Directors of the New Orleans Chapter of the Federal Bar Association, and he had been an active member of the Young Lawyers Section of the New Orleans Bar Association. He also is a member of the American Bar Association Title Insurance Litigation Committee. Mr. Balhoff is also an active member of St. Stephen Parish, and an officer in the Notre Dame Club of New Orleans. Mr. Balhoff enjoys spending time with his wife and three children.

attorneys.name: Ann Mallett Barker
attorneys.firm_name: Ann Mallett Barker, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Administration, Probate, Successions, Donations Lawyers in Lockport, LA
attorneys.bio:
After receiving my Juris Doctorate degree from Loyola University in New Orleans in 1984, I began practicing law in Houma, Louisiana at the well established law firm of Watkins, Walker, and Hermann. My relationship with that firm and its successor firms spanned several decades. I have practiced law in the areas of estate administration, medical malpractice defense, insurance defense, business litigation, employment discrimination, personal injury and business planning. In addition to the traditional practice of law, I spent several years in the early 1990's as a licensed insurance and investment counselor and several years post- Katrina as an in-house risk manager.

As a licensed practicing attorney in southeast Louisiana for over 30 years, I have gained a deep appreciation for Louisiana legal tradition, placing great importance on the orderly transfer of assets within families upon death. The value of a real estate inheritance in south Louisiana is heightened by the stark reality that our treasured way of life is intimately connected to our disappearing geography. I take great pleasure in assisting Louisiana families with estate transfers in the most cost effective manner possible.

Free consultations are available by appointment. Cost estimates can be provided following consultation.

attorneys.name: Carl Barkemeyer
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Baton Rouge, LA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Carl Barkemeyer and his staff have aggressively represented hundreds of criminally-charged clients throughout Louisiana, including Baton Rouge, Shreveport, Covington, Lafayette, Monroe, New Orleans, and many more. Attorney Barkemeyer's practice is focused primarily on defending the rights of the accused. He believes that in order to be an asset to a client with criminal charges, the attorney must be highly skilled at trial. Attorney Barkemeyer has spent his career developing, perfecting, and implementing his superior trial skills. Additionally, his practice includes assisting and/or consulting with other attorneys at civil and criminal trials. His assistance varies from strategic evidentiary advice to performing jury selection and/or cross-examinations.

attorneys.name: Ashley E. Bass
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Hammond, LA
attorneys.bio:
Ashley Edwards Bass, a Hammond native, obtained her Bachelor of Science degree in Psychology from Mississippi State in 1989. She then received her Juris Doctorate from Louisiana State University Law Center in 1996. From 1995-1997, she worked at the 21st Judicial District Court as a law clerk. She was admitted in 1996 to practice in Louisiana, and joined the firm in 1997. She became a partner in 2002. Ashley expanded her law expertise in 2018 by becoming a Mediator and Special Master with Mediation Arbitration Professional Systems, Inc. (maps). https://maps-adr.com/

During her undergraduate studies, she was a member of Chi Omega Sorority and appeared on both the Dean's and President's Lists.

Currently, Ashley is a member of the Louisiana State Bar Association, the Federal Bar Association, the Louisiana Association of Defense Counsel, and the 21st Judicial District Bar Association.

A former board member of CASA (Court Appointed Special Advocates) and of the Hammond Junior Auxiliary, Ashley remains active in community organizations. She served on the Board of the Hammond Chamber of Commerce as the co-chair of the Education Committee and the Steering Committee for the accelerated learning program. She was active in the development of the Magnet School Pilot Program. Ashley is also a past board member of the Tangipahoa Chapter of the American Cancer Society.

Ashley served on the Board of Trustees for the LSU Law School and was recently honored as a Trustee Emeritus for her years of service. She was named JA Woman of the Year and was most recently selected by the Tangipahoa Chamber of Commerce as a 2022 Annie Award recipient recognizing women who work in excellence and have a true servant’s heart for our community.

Ashley is a member of Holy Ghost Catholic Church in Hammond and served on the Holy Ghost School Board where she also served as Chairperson. She also served on the Baton Rouge Diocesan School Board.

﻿Ashley holds a Peer Review standing of ‘AV Preeminent', the highest possible review classification determined by reviews from others in the legal community and as listed in The LexisNexis Martindale-Hubbell Attorney Directory. Ashley was also voted Best Attorney in TANGI lifestyles Voted Readers' Choice best of 2021.

attorneys.name: Damon Louis Beard
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lake Charles, LA
attorneys.bio:
Damon Beard grew up in a blue collar family. His parents, David and Kathy, taught him that working hard was important and necessary to achieve success. Now, Damon is a partner at The Townsley Law Firm, proving his parents right.

Damon was raised in Moss Bluff, Louisiana, and went to Sam Houston High School. After high school, he went to Louisiana State University at Eunice where he obtained an associates degree in science. After graduation, he attended Louisiana State University, majoring in microbiology on the pre-med track.

Damon graduated from LSU with a bachelor’s degree in microbiology. He worked for a year and a half in an emergency room while considering whether to pursue a career in medicine or law.

In 2002, Damon ultimately decided to go to law school. He enrolled in Southern University Law Center and graduated in 2005. He then clerked with Judge Ward Fontenot in Cameron Parish, before he was invited to join The Townsley Law Firm.

Damon always knew that he wanted to help people, whether that be in the medical field or as a lawyer. At The Townsley Law Firm, he is able to utilize his medical background to help him have a better understanding of his cases, which makes him unique to the firm.

Early in Damon’s career, he was in the Young Lawyers Section and was on the board of the Southwest Louisiana Law Center. He is a past president and still participates as a board member of Crime Stoppers, an organization allowing people to send anonymous tips about unsolved and open crimes.

Outside of the office, Damon likes to hunt and fish. He also loves to stay active playing golf, tennis, and working out. Damon values his hobbies because they allow him to clear his mind and relieve stress.

Damon is married to his wife, Lori, and they have two kids, Jackson and Addison. His family motivates and inspires him to be successful. He strives to set a great example for his kids, so they can build upon his accomplishments in the future.

Throughout his years as an attorney, Damon has accumulated all of the skills needed to help his clients. Helping people and making sure they get the help they need is the reason he goes to work every day. Damon works to his full ability to get clients what they deserve and get them in the right state of mind for healing.

People trust Damon and the staff at TLF because they always strive for excellence when handling cases. They care about people and know that the job they are doing could change someone’s life. Damon and his team practice with the attitude to help clients, and continue to work for them, against all odds.

attorneys.name: Travis A. Beaton
attorneys.firm_name: Sher Garner Cahill Richter Klein & Hilbert, L.L.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
Travis Beaton is a Member of the Firm’s Business Section. Mr. Beaton’s principal areas of practice include all aspects of commercial real estate transactions, leasing, land use, finance, and general corporate matters. His experience includes representation of clients in connection with purchase and sale agreements, acquisitions and dispositions of real property, negotiated asset purchases, financing transactions, title and survey matters, commercial and retail leases, real estate development, and general commercial contracts. Mr. Beaton is also a licensed title insurance producer in the State of Louisiana, and an authorized agent for several title insurers. As a member of the Firm’s title agency, Capdevielle Title Corporation, Mr. Beaton’s extensive familiarity with title matters is a key component of his routine handling of estate transactions involving all types of properties, including multi-family residential, industrial, hospitality-based, mixed-use, apartment complexes, office buildings, luxury retail, shopping centers, and convenience centers. Mr. Beaton also has substantial experience with specialized telecommunication facilities leases, easements and related agreements, and frequently assists clients with federal trademark applications and registrations.

Mr. Beaton earned his undergraduate degree from Emory University, majoring in International Studies and minoring in Japanese. He earned his law degree from Tulane University Law School, graduating magna cum laude. While at Tulane, Mr. Beaton served as a Notes & Comments Editor for the Tulane Law Review, and as a Senior Fellow for the Legal Research & Writing Department. During law school, Mr. Beaton also served as an extern for Judge Susie Morgan of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana. He was awarded an academic scholarship, as well as the CALI Award for Excellence in Louisiana Successions, Donations & Trusts.

Mr. Beaton has served on Louisiana Bar Foundation’s Development Committee, and has been a member of the American Bar Association’s Real Property, Trusts & Estates Section since 2015, currently serving as a coeditor of the Section’s Probate & Property Magazine; Chair of the Leasing Group’s Ground Leasing Committee; and Co-Chair of the Section’s Joint Law Practice Management Group; and was a past vice-chair of the Commercial Real Estate Transactions’ Group’s Committee on Easements, Conditions, and Restrictions; as well as the Commercial Leasing Group’s Retail Leasing Committee. Mr. Beaton is an adjunct faculty member at Tulane University Law School, teaching a course in Real Estate Transactions, and frequently authors articles and prepares presentations relating to real property issues for various organizations and publications. He has been annually recognized by Best Lawyers for his work with Business Organizations, Corporate Law, and Real Estate law since 2021, and recognized by Louisiana Super Lawyers as a Rising Star in Real Estate since 2020.

attorneys.name: Tara E. Bell Hawkins
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Lake Charles, LA
attorneys.bio:
Tara Bell Hawkins' legal career has spanned 20 years. She is a skilled appellate advocate as well as an experienced trial lawyer with recognized courtroom advocacy abilities. Her focus at Hawkins Legal is criminal defense representation and family law.

Shortly after graduating from Tulane University School of Law in 1997, she embarked on a career in litigation and appeals. For more than ten years she worked as a corporate defense attorney at large Louisiana-based law firms. Ms. Hawkins discovered her passion for criminal law after embarking on a career as an assistant district attorney. During her career as a felony prosecutor, she successfully mastered prosecution of the most serious felony cases, including sex crimes, murders, and other complex, high-profile crimes. Because of her success and widely-recognized talents as a skilled trial lawyer, she was selected to lead her office's felony prosecution staff as its Chief Felony Prosecutor.

Hawkins' years of experience as a prosecutor heightened her sensitivity to the many inequities that still remain in the criminal justice system. She responded by creating a law firm that provides preeminent legal representation to individuals accused of crimes throughout Louisiana.

Nicholas A. Blanda represents clients throughout Louisiana, Texas and the Gulf Coast, specializing in serious personal injury and wrongful death cases arising from maritime/offshore accidents, trucking/18-wheeler accidents, automobile accidents, onshore/industrial accidents, products liability, and premises defect.

attorneys.name: Chet G. Boudreaux
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Baton Rouge, LA
attorneys.bio:
Chet Boudreaux, originally from Lafayette, Louisiana, graduated from St. Thomas More Catholic High School in 1994 and then went on to obtain his Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Southwestern Louisiana. In 2003, he received his law degree from Southern University, where he graduated Magna Cum Laude and obtained the Corporations Scholarship award. Chet joined McKernan Law Firm as a law clerk in 2001 and later became an Associate after passing the Bar. He is licensed to practice in all State and Federal courts in both Louisiana and Mississippi as well as the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. His diverse practice has afforded Chet the opportunity to assist numerous injured individuals in a wide variety of cases that resulting from incidents such as trucking accidents, automobile wrecks, 18-wheeler accidents, vehicle rollovers and many more. In all of Chet’s cases, the injuries suffered by his clients resulted from the negligence of another. Some of the injured clients Chet has successfully represented have suffered from spinal cord injuries, disk damage, burns, cancer (mesothelioma), and paralysis, just to name a few. In addition, Chet has represented clients all over the State of Louisiana including areas such as Lafayette, Lake Charles, Monroe, Shreveport, Plaquemine, Metairie and Prairieville; as well as in areas of Mississippi such as Hattiesburg, Jackson, and Gulfport. Chet has also played a major role in handling cases in Texas and in New Jersey and has been admitted pro hac vice to practice law in courts for the States of Arkansas, Florida and Texas. A few of Chet's most notable cases include a verdict of $2,855,000 in a custom bus wrongful death case, a verdict of $1.2 Million in a rear-end 18-wheeler accident and he recently settled two 18-wheeler cases for $950,000 and $875,000 respectively. Most recently, Chet has been selected for membership in The National Trial Lawyers Top 40 under 40 for the State of Louisiana.

Chet is married to Shanna Green of Rayville, Louisiana, and they have two children, Grayson, age 6 and Anna Grace, age 1. They are members of St. Jude Catholic Church. Chet enjoys hunting, fishing, horse racing and coaching t-ball for his son.

Chet joined McKernan Law Firm as a law clerk in 2001 and later became an Associate after passing the Bar. He is licensed to practice in all State and Federal courts in both Louisiana and Mississippi as well as the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. His diverse practice has afforded Chet the opportunity to assist numerous injured individuals in a wide variety of cases that resulting from incidents such as trucking accidents, automobile wrecks, 18-wheeler accidents, vehicle rollovers and many more. In all of Chet’s cases, the injuries suffered by his clients resulted from the negligence of another. Some of the injured clients Chet has successfully represented have suffered from spinal cord injuries, disk damage, burns, cancer (mesothelioma), and paralysis, just to name a few. In addition, Chet has represented clients all over the State of Louisiana including areas such as Lafayette, Lake Charles, Monroe, Shreveport, Plaquemine, Metairie and Prairieville; as well as in areas of Mississippi such as Hattiesburg, Jackson, and Gulfport. Chet has also played a major role in handling cases in Texas and in New Jersey and has been admitted pro hac vice to practice law in courts for the States of Arkansas, Florida and Texas. A few of Chet's most notable cases include a verdict of $2,855,000 in a custom bus wrongful death case, a verdict of $1.2 Million in a rear-end 18-wheeler accident and he recently settled two 18-wheeler cases for $950,000 and $875,000 respectively. Most recently, Chet has been selected for membership in The National Trial Lawyers Top 40 under 40 for the State of Louisiana.

Chet is married to Shanna Green of Rayville, Louisiana, and they have two children, Grayson, age 6 and Anna Grace, age 1. They are members of St. Jude Catholic Church. Chet enjoys hunting, fishing, horse racing and coaching t-ball for his son.

attorneys.name: Loyd J. Bourgeois
attorneys.firm_name: Loyd J Bourgeois Injury & Accident Lawyer
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in Luling, LA
attorneys.bio:
Loyd J. Bourgeois is a personal injury attorney and founder of the Louisiana-based law firm, Loyd J Bourgeois Injury & Accident Lawyer. Since opening his doors in 2010, Loyd has focused on helping injured individuals get the support and compensation they need after life-changing accidents. Whether it is a car crash, trucking accident, or other serious injury, his mission is to provide honest guidance and reliable representation during some of life’s most difficult moments.

Before becoming an attorney, Loyd worked as an engineer, a background that sharpened his problem-solving skills and attention to detail. But after witnessing how the insurance system often takes advantage of regular people, he made the decision to pursue law and graduated cum laude from Tulane University School of Law. That personal experience still drives him to fight for those who cannot fight for themselves.

Loyd has built a legal team known not just for results, but for compassion. His clients appreciate that he listens, explains the process clearly, and treats them like people, not just case files. Based in St. Charles Parish, LJBLegal serves clients throughout Southeast Louisiana and has become a trusted local name for those seeking justice after an injury.

When he is not working on behalf of his clients, Loyd stays active in the community he proudly calls home. He and his wife, Lindy, are raising their three children in St. Charles Parish and are involved in local schools, youth activities, and community events. For Loyd, being a lawyer is not just about courtrooms. It is about being there for his neighbors when they need him most.

attorneys.name: Stephen C. Braud
attorneys.practice_type: Probate & Successions Lawyers in Belle Chasse, LA
attorneys.bio:
STEPHEN C. BRAUD was born in Marksville, Louisiana in 1947. He was graduated from the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado in 1970 with a Bachelor of Science degree in Aeronautical Engineering. He received a Juris Doctorate degree from the Louisiana State University School of Law in 1978. In 1980, he co-founded the firm of Lobrano, Ballay & Braud, PLC, with Robert L. Lobrano, now Judge Retired, Fourth Circuit Court of Appeal, and Charles J. Ballay. Upon Robert Lobrano's election to the Bench, the firm name was changed to Ballay & Braud, PLC. Mr. Braud served as the Parish Attorney for the Plaquemines Parish Government in which capacity he established an in-house legal office and oversaw a staff of eight employees engaged in insurance defense, port authority matters, zoning, subdivision, permits & licenses, oil & gas landowner issues, sales tax, contract and general municipal law matters. He has appeared before the Louisiana State Mineral Board and the Louisiana Conservation Commission on various oil and gas matters. He has also appeared before the Louisiana Legislature on matters relating to minerals, zoning, elder law and municipal law. He has served on the Board for the Natural Resources Section of the Louisiana State Bar Association, and he is a charter member of the Governor's Task Force on Elder Law. He also has served as a Special Assistant Attorney General for the State of Louisiana in oil & gas ownership issues on State lands in Plaquemines Parish.

Mr. Braud is a member of the National Association of Elder Law Attorneys, the Plaquemines Bar Association, the Louisiana State Bar Association - where he served as a Member of the House of Delegates from 1993 to 2008, and the American Bar Association. In addition to his admission to practice in Louisiana, Mr. Braud is admitted before the U.S. District Court, Eastern, Middle and Western Districts of Louisiana, and the U.S. Court of Appeals, Fifth Circuit. He is a licensed title insurance agent for the national firm of Security Title Guaranty Corp. of Baltimore. Mr. Braud is married, is the father of two children, and the grandfather of five.

attorneys.name: S. Jacob Braud
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Belle Chasse, LA
attorneys.bio:
S. Jacob Braud began his legal career as a law clerk to Judge Robert A. Pitre, Jr. of the 24th Judicial District Court for the Parish of Jefferson in 2002, assisting with all aspects of both the civil and criminal dockets.

After completion of the judicial clerkship in 2003, he began a practice focusing on litigation and the defense of general torts, premises liability, medical and legal malpractice, and worker's compensation claims. Throughout this period, he represented several public entities including local governments, school boards, sheriffs' departments, their insurers, and excess insurers throughout Louisiana and Mississippi. Also, Jacob obtained significant experience representing large private corporations such as Wal-Mart, Best Buy, and Tenet Healthcare.

As an Appellate Litigator, Jacob has briefed or argued in each Louisiana Appellate Court and briefed several matters to the Louisiana Supreme Court.

In January 2009, Jacob came to Ballay, Braud & Colon commemorating the second generation to practice at the firm. In January 2013, he was elevated to the status of partner. Six years of litigation experience from a defense perspective has given Jacob a unique and invaluable skill to assess and assert the interests of injured clients. In addition to representing those injured through no fault of their own, Jacob began representing individuals and small businesses on a variety of matters such as contracts, liens, and acquisitions using his background in representing large corporations and governments to counsel clients through current and potential issues.

Additionally, Jacob expanded his legal practice by assisting the firm in its well-established real estate closing practice. Since 2009, he has produced title work and performed numerous real estate closings and created a separate title company, Arpent Title, LLC.

On April 20, 2010, the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill occurred greatly affecting many aspects of the community which Ballay, Braud & Colon has served for more than 40 years. Jacob served as the firm's lead liaison for the Court's Settlement Program. Ballay, Braud & Colon successfully represented a number of seafood industry claimants, businesses, individuals, and wetland landowners.

Jacob continues to represent and assist numerous residents and businesses in the metro area in a wide range of legal matters both simple and complex. He has also worked in development projects, including acquiring and permitting the 338-acre Jesuit Bend Mitigation Bank, the first in the State of Louisiana to use renewable materials and has successfully completed the zoning and permitting of the Parks of Plaquemines and Cypress Park Subdivisions, Plaquemines’ first master planned neighborhoods to provide amenities and greenspace.

Out of the office, Jacob is married to Erin O'Brien Braud and is the proud father of two daughters and one son.

attorneys.name: David D. Bravo
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
David Bravo’s training as an advocate began long before law school. In high school, David was a nationally competitive Cross Examination debater. He spent his summers learning to persuasively speak and research at prestigious institutions such as Dartmouth College, The University of Toledo, and Loyola University. He won the Louisiana High School State Championship and placed in the top ten at the City Championship three years in a row for Extemporaneous Speaking. In college, David won LSU’s Persuasive Speech Contest.

At Loyola Law School, David earned a scholarship as the swing oralist on the Moot Court National Team which required him to argue both sides of the issue. His team won the Regional Championship and finished fifth in the nation.

Immediately after graduation, David was baptized by fire as he worked as a prosecutor in Orleans Parish. He quickly rose to Senior Trial Attorney and began handling serious felony cases, including death penalty cases. David tried nearly a hundred cases as a prosecutor, including three jury trials in just one day.

After leaving the DA’s office, David worked for a downtown insurance defense firm. During this period, David learned how insurance companies evaluate cases. He also learned that his personal satisfaction came from representing people, not big insurance companies.

For the last 12 years, David has represented only individuals and small companies. He has used his experience in evaluating and trying cases to achieve justice for his clients. He continues to actively train as an advocate. He recently spent a month at the Trial Lawyer’s College at Thunderhead Ranch in Wyoming, founded by famed trial lawyer Gerry Spence. David has also taught Trial Skills Courses at Loyola Law School.

David would be happy to meet with you to see if his unique set of skills can help you with your current challenge.

attorneys.name: Arthur J. Brewster
attorneys.practice_type: Longshore, Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, Defense Base Act Lawyers in Metairie, LA
attorneys.bio:
I have been practicing law since 1987 after graduating from Loyola Law School in New Orleans. Prior to starting my own firm, I practiced with local law firms that represented various injured works and handled general maritime claims, as well as personal injury claims. More than 20 years ago, I started my own firm to focus my practice on representing injured workers. Over my career, I have had the pleasure of representing injured men, women, and their families for various types of injuries under the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act, the Defense Base Act, the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, the Jones Act, personal injury claims, and general maritime claims. I have handled cases before the DOL, the Office of Administrative Law Judges, the Benefits Review Board, and the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. I have additionally tried numerous bench and jury trials in various state and federal district courts.

I am a frequent lecturer on topics that arise under the Defense Base Act and Longshore Act. I regularly participate in the Annual Loyola Longshore Conference, and I am a member the Loyola Longshore Conference Advisory Board. I have presented numerous Continuing Legal Education seminars to other attorneys on the Longshore and Defense Base Act. In 2016 WILG, a national advocacy group for injured workers, presented me with the WILG Longshore/DBA Excellence in Practice Award. I have the highest rating with Martindale-Hubbell for legal skills and ethics.

I have been married for 30 years to my wife Jamee. We have three sons. When not working, I enjoy salt-water fishing and sporting events.

My practice deals almost exclusively with representing injury workers in stevedoring, shipbuilding and ship-repair, and the offshore oil industry. I additionally represent numerous injured contractors for United States government working abroad. I handle general maritime claims and personal injury claims as well.

I have presented Continuing Legal Educations seminars to other attorneys. I am a member of the Workers Injury Law and Advocacy Group, the Joint DOL Bar Association, and the St. Thomas More Inn of Court.

When not practicing law, I enjoy spending time with my wife and sailing.

attorneys.name: Aaron J. Broussard
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lake Charles, LA
attorneys.bio:
Aaron is a life-long resident of Sulphur, Louisiana. He graduated from Sulphur High School in 1998 and graduated from McNeese four years later. He attended Tulane Law School in New Orleans, and began practicing law at the age of 25.

In law school, Aaron was a lead member of Tulane’s National Moot Court Trial Team. He was also selected for Tulane’s Law Clinic which allows senior students to represent real clients while still in school. Aaron dedicated his law clinic experience to assisting victims of domestic violence in New Orleans. He also graduated with a Certificate of Specialization in Maritime Law.

Aaron recently graduated from Gerry Spence's Trial Lawyers College. Gerry Spence is widely accepted as the greatest trial lawyer for the people alive today. The Trial Lawyers College is an intense four week program dedicated to helping lawyers learn how to represent people against the powers of the government, corporations, and the insurance industry.

The college is held at Gerry Spence's ranch in the mountains near Dubois, Wyoming. Every week, a fresh staff of the best attorneys he has ever met came to the Ranch to teach you what they have learned from years of experience. The Trial Lawyers College method is not about teaching lawyers how to trick juries into giving money. It is about getting to know your clients on a personal level and discovering the real story of their case. A lawyer cannot tell a story they do not know or understand.

Many people complain that their lawyers do not listen to them and do not respect them as people. They are just another file. Even before Aaron went to the Trial Lawyers College, he communicated with clients with courtesy and respect because it was the right thing to do. Aaron has always believed you must treat others how you would like to be treated. Now more than ever, he is eager to get to know his client and their story. Aaron only accepts a limited number of cases, so that he can give each client and each story the time and dedication they deserve. If you do not want to get to know your lawyer or you are looking to settle your case quickly and for less than you deserve, he may not be the best lawyer for you.

Aaron currently lives in Lake Charles. In his spare time, Aaron stays outside enjoying tennis, hunting, and fishing.

At this point, the majority of Aaron’s practice is dedicated to helping victims of serious personal injury arising from automobile accidents, medical malpractice, and products liability.

attorneys.name: Douglas D. Brown
attorneys.firm_name: The Douglas Brown Law Firm, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Hammond, LA
attorneys.bio:
Douglas D. Brown, Attorney at Law, is a husband and is a father of three, and has practiced Criminal defense and family law in Tangiphoa Parish for nearly two decades. After working in Washington, D.C. for Congressman Richard Baker, Brown served as a judicial law clerk for State District Judges Ray Chutz in Amite and M. Douglas Hughes in Livingston. He later served as the City of Hammond's Assistant City Prosecutor. Before earning a JD degree at Louisiana State University's Paul M. Hebert Law Center, Brown attended Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. and earned a BA degree from Southeastern Louisiana University in Economics.

Brown's felony trial practice includes homicide, drug trafficking, kidnapping, burglary, and DWI.

Brown has been a member of the American Bar Association, the Federal Bar Association, the Louisiana State Bar Association, the Louisiana Association for Criminal Defense Lawyers, The Twenty First Judicial District Bar Association, and the Florida Parishes Inns of Court.

In his spare time, Brown is a Little League Coach for the Hammond City Recreation Department. He is also the Hammond Eastside Magnet PTA Vice President, and has been a CASA Volunteer Trainer.

attorneys.firm_name: Roedel Parsons Koch Blache Balhoff & McCollister
attorneys.practice_type: General Litigation Lawyers in Baton Rouge, LA
attorneys.bio:
Ryan's career started as a law clerk with the Louisiana Department of Justice, Attorney General's Office, Criminal Division where he was involved in the drafting and preparation of Louisiana Attorney General Opinions and pleadings. After graduation, Ryan became an associate with Urbach, Hacker, and Young Advisors assisting corporate clients in the area of state and local income and franchise and property (SALT) tax.

At Roedel Parsons, Ryan has a diverse practice in the area of General Litigation, Corporate Law, Wills & Successions, Business Transactions, Landlord & Tenant Law, Ad Volarem Tax Law, and Family Law.

Ryan's passion is giving back to the community. He currently serves with various programs affiliated with the Baton Rouge Bar Association, some of which include Ask-A-Lawyer, Family Law Self-Help Resource Center, Holiday Star Committee, Junior Partners Academy Committee, Law Day Committee, and Pro Bono Individual Bankruptcy Representation. Ryan is also a volunteer high school basketball coach. Ryan further serves as Chairman of Just Cause LA, Inc., a nonprofit corporation serving residents of Baton Rouge and surrounding areas.

Ryan has been recognized for his outstanding service to his community by receiving the Baton Rouge Bar Association President's Award (2013), the Louisiana State Bar Association Young Lawyers Division Pro Bono Award (2013) and the Judge Joseph Keogh Memorial Award (2014).

Ryan received his Bachelor of Science in Business Information Technology from Louisiana State University and his Juris Doctorate - Bachelor of Law (Common\Civil Law) from Paul M. Hebert Law Center, Louisiana State University.

attorneys.name: Christian T. Bruno
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
Christian T. Bruno represents the third generation of lawyers in the Bruno family. He began his journey in the legal field at the age of 14, assisting with filing at Bruno & Bruno during summer breaks. A native of New Orleans, Christian graduated from Jesuit High School in 2014. He then attended the University of Colorado in Boulder, where he majored in Philosophy and Psychology. His studies were driven by a passion for mental health and human behavior. During his time in Colorado, Christian worked for the CU Institute of Behavioral Science.

After earning his undergraduate degree in 2019, Christian returned to New Orleans and began working as an intern at the Jefferson Parish District Attorney’s Office. He enrolled at Loyola University College of Law in the same year and graduated in 2023. Christian sought diverse experiences throughout law school, including a summer internship at the Conroy Law Firm in Metairie, Louisiana, which broadened his perspective on legal defense. After successfully passing the Louisiana Bar in 2023, Christian joined Bruno & Bruno as an associate attorney. He now works alongside his brother, father, uncle, and cousin. Beyond his legal endeavors, Christian is committed to service, particularly in the areas of mental health and addiction. He continues to dedicate his efforts to enhancing the community's well-being and quality of life in New Orleans.

attorneys.name: Joseph M. Bruno Sr.
attorneys.practice_type: Liability Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
Joseph M. Bruno is widely regarded as a creative, energetic and outspoken advocate of victims’ rights, particularly in difficult and complex cases of liability. He is a defender of class action procedures, seeing them as an important balancing tool in our complex society. He is a graduate of Tulane University and Tulane Law School (1978). In 1979, he went into partnership with his father, Frank S. Bruno, a well-known and respected litigator, most particularly in the field of workers’ compensation.

Joseph Bruno has been admitted to practice in all courts in Louisiana and Texas, as well as the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Middle Districts of Louisiana, the United States 5th Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Tax Court.

Joseph Bruno is recognized as an authority in class actions and particularly in class action management. His expertise in difficult and complex litigation has led to his representation of numerous claimants in class action and mass joinder proceedings involving racial discrimination, occupational lung disease, product liability, and wage and hour violations.

Joseph Bruno has been active in the Louisiana Trial Lawyers Association, having served on the Board of Governors for over 20 years. His goal is to build and maintain an aggressive firm that has the courage to fund and handle all types of complex and difficult litigation.

attorneys.name: Stephen P. Bruno
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
Over the last 40 years, Stephen has successfully handled over 5,000 cases, recovering over $100 million in verdicts and settlements for his clients. Although Stephen has placed a special emphasis on maritime personal injury, he has used his trial skills to obtain successful judgments in a variety of civil cases, including successions, oil and gas, wrongful death, product liability, automobile accidents, premises liability, defamation and slip-and-falls.

He has lectured at seminars for the Louisiana Trial Lawyers Association and has been recognized as a diplomat by the American Association for Justice in trial advocacy. Stephen is a member of the Louisiana Association for Justice, the American Association for Justice and the New Orleans Bar Association and is a past president of the St. Thomas More Catholic Lawyers Association. Stephen was recognized as a Leader in Law by New Orleans Magazine, AV rated by Martindale Hubbell , annually named one of the Top Lawyers in New Orleans and one of the top attorneys In America.

In addition to his law practice, Stephen served as Custodian of the Notarial Records for the Parish of Orleans and served as chairman of the Notarial Examination Committee for Orleans Parish. He served in those capacities from 1992-1996 and 2004-2009 and is the only custodian to be nonconsecutively appointed by two Louisiana governors. He was responsible for initiating digital scanning of original acts to make them available on the internet.

Stephen is active in civic affairs and has served as president of his neighborhood association, spearheaded fund-raising activities for religious and academic institutions and is a past president of the St. Rita Parish Council.

Stephen is a member of the Louisiana Association for Justice, the American Association for Justice and the New Orleans Bar Association and is a past president of the St. Thomas More Catholic Lawyers Association. Stephen was recognized as a Leader in Law by New Orleans Magazine, AV rated by Martindale Hubbell , annually named one of the Top Lawyers in New Orleans and one of the top attorneys In America.

In addition to his law practice, Stephen served as Custodian of the Notarial Records for the Parish of Orleans and served as chairman of the Notarial Examination Committee for Orleans Parish. He served in those capacities from 1992-1996 and 2004-2009 and is the only custodian to be nonconsecutively appointed by two Louisiana governors. He was responsible for initiating digital scanning of original acts to make them available on the internet.

Stephen is active in civic affairs and has served as president of his neighborhood association, spearheaded fund-raising activities for religious and academic institutions and is a past president of the St. Rita Parish Council.

attorneys.name: R. Scott Buhrer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Metairie, LA
attorneys.bio:
Scott Buhrer is a long time resident of Kenner, Louisiana. He attended Tulane University where he received a B.A. in political science (1982), his law degree (1986) and a Masters of Business Administration (MBA) (1995). After law school, Mr. Buhrer worked briefly at a large, downtown law firm. Mr. Buhrer subsequently served for three (3) years as an Assistant City Attorney in New Orleans while also employed with an established family law firm where he obtained his training in this specialized area of the law from one of the then foremost experts in the field.

A seasoned trial attorney and negotiator, Mr. Buhrer brings over 24 years experience to every family law and succession matter he handles. Clients can count on his perspective and understanding to guide them effectively through the legal process and arrive at a successful resolution of their legal problems. Mr. Buhrer has worked on literally hundreds of cases in the family law and succession areas during his career, ranging from simple, non-contested matters to extremely complex and highly contentious cases. As a sole practitioner, he personally handles every aspect of each case and keeps clients informed every step of the way.

In recognition of his legal knowledge and experience and his reputation amongst Judges and other lawyers, Mr. Buhrer is frequently appointed by family law Judges in Jefferson, St. Tammany and Orleans Parishes to serve as Special Master in difficult and complex family law matters. In that capacity, he makes formal recommendations to the Trial Judge, which if not objected to, become the ruling of the Court. Only a select few family law practitioners are appointed to this important position.

Mr. Buhrer also maintains the highest possible AV Preeminent peer review rating by Martindale Hubbell and has been named a Top Lawyer in the area of Family Law by New Orleans Magazine.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lake Charles, LA
attorneys.bio:
Joe Burke is a native of New Iberia, Louisiana. His areas of practice include personal injury, criminal law, family law and successions. While his primary office is here in Lake Charles, Joe still maintains an office in New Iberia office to service clients in his hometown.

Prior to attending law school, Joe received undergraduate and graduate degrees in geography from LSU and the University of Maryland. He worked with the United States Navy, Department of Commerce, several foreign governments, and in the public sector on numerous hydrographic surveying projects creating modern nautical charts and responding to navigational catastrophes. Joe is proud to have surveyed the least depth on Bligh Reef, the reef in Prince William Sound, Alaska, notorious for its role in the Exxon Valdez tragedy.

Joe earned his J.D./D.C.L. from Louisiana State University, where he was a member of LSU's Admiralty Moot Court and Trial Advocacy Teams, served as Vice-President of the Trial Advocacy Board, and won the prestigious Ira S. Flory Trial Competition. He is a member of the Louisiana Bar Association, the Louisiana Association for Justice, and the Southwest Louisiana Bar Association.

After graduating from Loyola College Prep in 2005, she headed off to Jackson, MS to attend Millsaps College where she majored in Religious Studies, minored in Psychology, and was a Lilly Fellow. As a Lilly Fellow, she completed an externship at Mississippi Families for Kids, a fellowship at the Hinds County District Attorney's Office, and a leadership project at Matt's House Emergency Shelter for Women and Children. Amber graduated from Millsaps magna cum laude in 2009 and was inducted into the Phi Beta Kappa Honor Society.

Eager to gain the tools to make a difference, in 2009, Amber began law school at the LSU Paul M. Hebert Law Center. During her law school career she completed a summer clerkship at the Office of the Louisiana Attorney General in the Criminal Appellate Division, an externship at the East Baton Rouge Parish District Attorney's Office in the Domestic Violence Section, and an externship at the Baton Rouge Battered Women's Program in the Legal Services Component. She also worked as a law clerk at Akers & Wisbar and participated as a Certified Student Attorney in the LSU Juvenile Defense Clinic.

Amber graduated from law school in May of 2012, she sat for the Louisiana State Bar Exam in July of 2012, and she was sworn in to practice in October of 2012. Her desire is to serve the Louisiana community as an advocate for families, children, and victims of abuse. She enjoys doing adoptions, estate planning, family law, protective orders, and successions.

Amber currently resides in New Orleans with her husband, Chris, and their son. She is an active member of the Louisiana State Bar Association, the New Orleans Bar Association, the Jefferson Bar Association, the Junior League of New Orleans, and Power of Women. She currently serves on both the Children's Law Committee and the Public Access and Consumer Protection Committee for the Louisiana State Bar Association. She enjoys cooking, reading, shopping, traveling, and spending time with family, friends, and her dog, Annabelle.

attorneys.name: Elwood F. Cahill Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Sher Garner Cahill Richter Klein & Hilbert, L.L.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Real Estate Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Cahill is a member of the Firm's Business Group whose practice is concentrated in commercial real estate, business and finance law, as well as creditors' rights, workouts and foreclosures and commercial bankruptcy and other commercial transactions. Mr. Cahill practices before and works closely with political entities and public administrative boards and agencies at the local, parish (county) and state levels. Mr. Cahill is also a licensed title insurance agent in the State of Louisiana.

As part of his practice, Mr. Cahill is actively involved with many professional and trade organizations, including the American Bar Association’s Section of Business Law where he previously served as Chair of the Real Estate Financing Subcommittee of the Commercial Finance Committee), the ABA's Real Property Probate & Trust Law Section (where he previously served as a Supervisory Council Member of the Section's Governing Council, as well as Chair of the Section’s Diversity Committee), the ABA’s Torts and Insurance (TIPS) Section (where he has served as Vice Chair of that Section’s Title Insurance Litigation Committee), the American College of Real Estate Lawyers, the American Bankruptcy Institute, and the International Council of Shopping Centers, a trade association that represents the interests of those involved in the shopping center industry. Mr. Cahill is a past president of the Louisiana Bar Foundation, as well as a past member of the Board of Directors of the New Orleans Bar Association. Mr. Cahill also serves on the Loyola Law School Visiting Committee, whose purpose is to serve as an advisory and consultative group to the Dean of the Law School, bringing the perspective of alumni and other friends of the Law School to bear on matters of Law School policy, activities, programs and goals, and acts as an advocate to assist the Dean in advancing the interest of the school.

Mr. Cahill is actively involved with many civic and charitable organizations, having served as Chair member of the Board of Directors of Children's Hospital in New Orleans, and on the Board of Directors of Louisiana Appleseed. He served as Co-Chair of the University of New Orleans Business Alumni Council, whose purpose is to serve as an advisory group to the Dean of the Business School to assist the Dean in advancing the interests of the School.

Mr. Cahill has taught as an Adjunct Professor (1993) and as a Skills Instructor (1992-2007) at Loyola Law School in New Orleans. He has spoken at numerous seminars, conventions and meetings throughout the country, including the American College of Real Estate Lawyers, American College of Mortgage Attorneys, American Bar Association, Louisiana State Bar Association, the New Orleans Bar Association, Louisiana Land Title Association and Louisiana Bankers Association, among other professional and trade groups.

attorneys.name: Robert L. Campbell
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Baton Rouge, LA
attorneys.bio:
Robb Campbell is rated AV by Martindale Hubbell and is a 2002 graduate of the Louisiana State University Paul M. Hebert Law Center. He is a member of the Louisiana State and Federal Bar Associations. Mr. Campbell focuses his practice primarily on personal injury, employment related cases, and workers' compensation cases. Mr. Campbell has represented clients in numerous auto accident cases, premises liability cases, and employment and workers' compensation cases. Mr. Campbell advises and represents clients on a variety of Employment issues including discrimination, harassment, and retaliation; issues involving the EEOC and Louisiana's Department of Labor; the ADA, FLSA, FMLA, and Title VII; state employment laws regarding employment discrimination, wage payment, worker's compensation, and unemployment compensation; and issues involving employment contracts. Mr. Campbell has a special interest in workers' compensation and employment law cases and has represented clients throughout Louisiana.

Robb has been named to the 2012 Louisiana Rising Stars list as one the the top up-and-coming attorneys in Louisiana for 2012. Each year, no more than 2.5 percent of the lawyers in the state receive this honor. The selection for this respected list is made by the research team at Super Lawyers.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Baton Rouge, LA
attorneys.bio:
Chris Cascio is a native of Bossier City, Louisiana. He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science from Louisiana State University in 1993. In 1996, he received his Juris Doctorate from Louisiana State University - Paul M. Hebert School of Law.

After his graduation from law school, Chris began his legal career as a judicial law clerk for Judge James T. Genovese of the 27th Judicial District Court in Parish of St. Landry. After completing his one year clerkship with Judge Genevose, Chris practiced in New Orleans, Louisiana focusing in the areas of insurance defense and litigation.

In 2001, Chris returned to Baton Rouge began his private practice representing individuals in personal injury, workers' compensation, family and criminal matters. Chris is committed to providing each and every client with vigorous, competent and effective representation.

Chris is licensed to practice before the Supreme Court of Louisiana and all of the appellate and district courts of Louisiana, the United States District Court for the Middle District of Louisiana and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit.

attorneys.name: Sean Michael Casey
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Hammond, LA
attorneys.bio:
Sean Michael Casey, a native of St. Charles Parish, graduated as the valedictorian of Destrehan High School's Class of 1983 before attending Louisiana State University where he earned a Bachelor of Science in Accounting completing the degree requirements in just three years while making the Dean's list most semesters. Sean attended LSU Law School graduating in 1989 and finishing in the top 20% of his class. While still in law school, Sean was recruited by a large defense firm in New Orleans where, after passing the Bar, he worked on multi-million dollar deals in the firm's commercial transactions section. With a focus on residential and commercial real estate acquisitions and financings, Sean went on to open and operate Louisiana's very first statewide title company that regularly served all 64 parishes, served as a compliance officer and vice president of Louisiana's largest bank holding company, and was the Director of Louisiana Operations for a title company owned in part by a Fortune 500 company.

Sean served on the school boards of Mater Dolorosa School in Independence (3 years) and St. Thomas Aquinas Regional Catholic High School in Hammond (7 years) and, also, served on the fair committee of Holy Ghost Catholic in Hammond (10 years). Sean proposed and then chaired a Diocesan committee that brought special education classrooms to a handful of Catholic schools throughout the Diocese of Baton Rouge after three years of careful planning and preparation.

Sean is a member of the Louisiana Bar Association and is admitted to practice in all Louisiana state courts as well as the U.S. District Courts of the Eastern, Middle, and Western Districts of Louisiana.

Sean, his wife, Rachel, and their daughter, Madison, have resided in Independence, Louisiana since 2000 when they purchased the farm they still call home. Sean's hobbies include traveling, riding his horses, raising miniature donkeys, snow skiing, golfing, and sharing time with family. From 2018 to early 2022, Sean and Rachel operated a bed & breakfast in Natchez, Mississippi. Sean joined Cashe Coudrain & Bass as an "of counsel" in 2022.

attorneys.name: David Grant Castillo
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Lake Charles, LA
attorneys.bio:
For most of his life, Grant Castillo grew up in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. He attended high school at Bethany Christian School, where he played basketball and baseball. After high school, Grant played baseball for Louisiana State University at Eunice, then Southern University.

Grant’s first dream was to be a baseball coach after watching his dad, David, coach high school basketball growing up. After his playing career ended in 2013, Grant moved to Lake Charles to be an assistant baseball coach at Barbe High School.

Grant coached alongside head coach Glenn Cecchini until 2018, winning three state championships and one national championship during his time there. His coaching career introduced him to Todd Townsley, who hired Grant to run errands at The Townsley Law Firm while he finished school and coached.

In 2016, while coaching at Barbe, Grant enrolled at McNeese State University, majoring in general studies. Determined to pursue a new dream of attending law school, Grant graduated from McNeese in December of 2018.

Grant attended law school at Southern University Law Center. There, he was top of his class and graduated Magna Cum Laude in 2021. Shortly after graduation, Grant began working for The Townsley Law Firm.

The Townsley Law Firm’s goal is to put the needs of their clients first, make clients feel comfortable, and give them first-class representation. The firm’s culture and team approach have made Grant a better lawyer. His personal experience of his father’s death due to medical malpractice gives him a unique perspective and empathy for the people he represents.

Outside of work, Grant loves spending time with his wife and children, playing golf, and watching football. All of these things help Grant clear his mind and relax.

Grant and his wife, Kaitlin, have two kids, Marie-Louise and David. He is thankful that he is able to make his family proud and continues to excel with their support. Grant is influenced by the mentorship of his dad, David, Glenn Cecchini, and Todd Townsley, who helped him achieve his goals and be in a position to make a positive impact on his client’s lives every day.

Grant works hard and fiercely represents his clients in their time of need. Helping people and having a positive impact with his clients is why he continues to work every day. Grant relies on the competitive mindset and work ethic he developed during his athletic and coaching career to win for his clients.

attorneys.name: Lisa Causey
attorneys.firm_name: Salim Beasley Causey Deblieux Attorneys at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Mass Tort Lawyers in Natchitoches, LA
attorneys.bio:
Lisa Causey-Streete was born and raised in Natchitoches, Louisiana, where she now practices with Salim Beasley Causey Deblieux Attorneys at Law. Lisa has substantial experience in mass tort pharmaceutical and medical device products liability litigation. She is an active member of the bar in Louisiana and Texas, and has focused almost exclusively on mass tort pharmaceutical and medical device products liability litigation since joining Salim Beasley Causey Deblieux Attorneys at Law in March 2012. The first ten years of Lisa's practice was spent as a defense attorney at prestigious firms in Houston, Texas and Beaumont, Texas involving medical malpractice, products liability, and a wide array of other personal injury cases. Uniquely, Lisa obtained her masters in health law in 2009 from the University of Houston's Health Law & Policy Institute in addition to her juris doctorate from South Texas College of Law in Houston in 2002, and bachelor of arts from Baylor University. Lisa is admitted to all United States District Courts in Texas and Louisiana as well as the United States Court of Appeals, Fifth Circuit.

On April 10, 2017, Lisa was appointed to the Plaintiffs' Executive Committee in In Re: Eliquis (Apixaban) Products Liability Action, MDL 2754, pending in the Southern District of New York before Judge Denise Cote. She also served on the Plaintiffs steering committee for the Eliquis case.

Currently, Lisa serves as the lead attorney handling the following cases for Salim Beasley Causey Deblieux Attorneys at Law:

Eliquis

Xarelto

Pradaxa

BP

Transvaginal Mesh

Lisa also handles many of Salim Beasley Causey Deblieux Attorneys at Law other personal injury cases arising from medical malpractice, car wrecks, and other catastrophic personal injuries.

Lisa is married to Jon B. Streete originally from Lake Charles, Louisiana. They were blessed with twins in March 2014: Jon Barton Streete and Jolie Kathern Streete. Lisa is a member of the First United Methodist Church in Natchitoches, Service League of Natchitoches, and is a board member for the Cane River's Children's home.

attorneys.name: Larry J. Centola
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action/Mass Torts Lawyers in New Orleans, LA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Centola focuses on class actions, products liability, and mass torts. Mr. Centola is class counsel in the Bayou Corne sinkhole lawsuit and has been named class counsel in medical billing lawsuits across the state against health care providers including a class action against Acadian Ambulance that settled for $5.9 million. Mr. Centola has represented victims of Chinese Drywall, victims of asbestos and silica exposure, and victims of faulty drugs and medical devices. In 2010, Mr. Centola received a favorable jury verdict for a man against an offshore drilling rig owner for exposing the man to mercury.

Mr. Centola has lectured across Louisiana on class actions, ethics, and professionalism.

Mr. Centola received his law degree from Louisiana State University in 2001 and his undergraduate degree from Louisiana State University in 1998. Mr. Centola served as the LSU Student Body President for the 1997-98 academic year and currently serves on the LSU Law Center Young Alumni Council.

After spending one year as a law clerk at the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana. Mr. Centola spent over five years at a major New Orleans defense firm before joining Martzell and Bickford in 2007.

Mr. Centola is a past Chairman of the Louisiana State Bar Association – Young Lawyers Section, he serves on the Executive Board of Directors for the New Orleans Chapter of the Federal Bar Association, and he is an active member of the Louisiana Association for Justice.

Mr. Centola is the 2008 recipient of the Sandra Day O'Conner Award for Professional Service, awarded by the national American Inns of Court to one young lawyer each year for excellence in pro bono activities.

In 2013, Mr. Centola won the President's Award from the Louisiana Association for Justice for dedicated service in the legal profession.
